_comment: SPEC COVERAGE REGISTRY (RENAR §8.4.1, ADR-023 §5). Per SPEC: the ENUMERABLE SET that constitutes its subject, and the enumerator that produces that set from the LIVE code. scripts/spec_completeness.py asks whether the body names every member. This is by SUBJECT, never by vocabulary: ADR-023 §4 rejects a blacklist of adjectives because the same words are legitimate when they name a property OF the subject and illegitimate when they narrow what must be described. An adjective removes no member, so a body may call one element 'the critical one' and stay green; a body describing four of seven guarded keys is red however neutrally it is phrased. A SPEC with no entry here is reported UNCHECKED by name, not passed. Adding a SPEC means adding a line here. See task nothing-checks-completeness-of-a-spec-body.
_reach: This control can cover 9 of the standard's 11 SPEC types. SPEC-TEST and SPEC-DOC do not exist in our closed list (service_specs.SPEC_TYPES), so reporting 'all types covered' would be the exact narrowing §8.4.1 forbids. Widening it is the task spec-closed-list-is-nine-while-the-standard-has-eleven, linked as a dependency in the DB.
